rejected_rule.statement: When considering whether a testator knew and approved of the contents of the will, the Court should take into consideration as a circumstance of suspicion that the party who wrote or prepared the will takes a benefit under it. However, this is not to be considered more than a circumstance of suspicion.
rejected_rule.supporting_quote: "Further, with regard to the nature and degree of proof that is required, the testator's instructions for, or reading over, the instrument are not the only satisfactory description of proof by which the cognizance of the contents of the will may be brought home to the deceased. A party who prepared a will under which he takes a benefit is a circumstance which ought generally to excite the suspicion of the Court and calls upon it to be vigilant and jealous in examining the evidence in support of the instrument."
